items.stem: You have a folder of identically structured monthly CSV files and want one combined table that updates when a new file is added. What is the Power Query approach?

options.text: Connect to the folder and combine/append the files, then refresh
options.rationale: Correct: a folder query consolidates matching files and picks up new ones on refresh.

options.text: Copy and paste each file into a sheet by hand
options.rationale: That is manual and not repeatable.

options.text: Email each file to yourself and merge in the body
options.rationale: That is not a data-transformation method.

items.explanation: Correct: a folder query consolidates matching files and picks up new ones on refresh.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Power Query are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Applied Steps record each transformation and replay on refresh
options.rationale: Correct: the recorded steps make the query repeatable.

options.text: Unpivot turns wide cross-tab columns into tidy rows
options.rationale: Correct: unpivoting is the standard reshape for cross-tabs.

options.text: Changes must be redone manually every time data changes
Power Query can only read a single worksheet
options.rationale: It connects to files, folders, workbooks, databases and the web.

items.explanation: Correct: the recorded steps make the query repeatable.

items.stem: A merge between Orders and Customers returns fewer rows than Orders had. Which join most likely caused this and what is the safer default when you want to keep all orders?

options.text: An inner join dropped unmatched orders; a left outer join keeps all orders
options.rationale: Correct: inner joins keep only matches, whereas a left outer join preserves every order.

options.text: A left outer join dropped them; switch to inner
options.rationale: That is backwards; inner drops unmatched rows.

options.text: Append caused it; use merge instead
options.rationale: Append stacks rows and would not reduce order count this way.

options.text: Type change caused it; remove all type changes
options.rationale: A type change does not drop rows based on matching.

items.explanation: Correct: inner joins keep only matches, whereas a left outer join preserves every order.
